speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; can you describe exactly what the spinning sensation feels like and if it is triggered by head movements? Also, have you experienced any nausea, hearing loss, or tinnitus alongside this?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The short duration of your spinning sensation (3 minutes) and the fact that you have returned to baseline without lingering hearing loss or neurological deficits are highly characteristic of BPPV. Given the sudden onset and lack of other concerning symptoms, I believe this is the most likely cause. Would you like me to perform the Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm this diagnosis?
